thread:
maria: Quick summary from the EUW1 incident earlier — posting raw notes so we have a single thread.
maria: What happened: GPU pools experienced near-OOM pressure for ~18m. Root trigger was a network fanout stall in euw1 that caused request backpressure. Autoscaler logic then funneled many queued long-chat sessions to the same AZ nodes, KV cache retained large contexts, and memory rose until OOM signals started firing. Throttling/fallbacks kicked in and we served degraded throughput.
alex: Can you paste the timeline and the specific autoscaler decision that put those pods together?
maria: Timeline (rough):
- 12:02: health check started showing elevated egress latency on the 3 euw1 ToR switches
- 12:05: router fanout retries increased; request latencies climbed for streaming RPCs
- 12:07: autoscaler saw sustained queue depth and created scale-up tasks but due to AZ weight config it placed many new containers in the same AZ to minimize cross-AZ egress
- 12:09: KV cache retention logic kept prefix caches warm -> memory per container ~ +3.2GB
- 12:12: kernel OOM notifications on two nodes, eviction attempts, then throttling and model fallback
- 12:20: traffic rerouted to euw2 and partial recovery
jamal: Did we have any promo/traffic churn around that time? I remember a marketing push earlier.
maria: Yes — a targeted EU marketing email went out at 11:55 which increased mid-tail chat sessions (longer contexts). Our forecast had assumed average session length 1.3k tokens but observed median ~3.7k for that cohort.
kai: So two compounding errors: underestimated session length in forecast + autoscaler AZ placement heuristics. Also the ToR network problem was the proximate hardware trigger.
sophia: Any evidence of KV cache leakage vs expected retention? Could be a bug keeping caches pinned across model restarts.
maria: We looked. Cache metrics show eviction requests were issued but the slow network increased RPC latency to the cache store and those evictions fell behind. No code leak detected; behavior matches degraded eviction rate under network stalls.
alex: Logs/snippet for the OOM events?
maria: Pasting the minimal log block we correlated (sanitized):
```
[12:11:43] node-12 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (model_worker) score 567
[12:11:44] model_worker[4123]: trying to free KV cache entry: 0x7f3abc.. 
[12:11:44] autoscaler: scale_up decision: +6 replicas -> placement: az-eu-west-1a (weight=0.8)
[12:11:46] kubelet: Eviction threshold crossed: memory.available < 150Mi
```
jamal: Are these node types the dense-gpu-1 (A100 80GB) or standard (H100 80GB) pools? Cost discussion soon.
maria: This affected dense-gpu-1 pool (A100) where most long-chat traffic currently lands for latency/seq reasons.
kai: Immediate mitigations we applied:
- lowered AZ placement weight so new pods spread across AZs (12:13)
- temporarily reduced long-chat concurrency cap per node (12:14)
- forced small TTL on KV cache entries in euw1 pool (12:15)
- traffic-split to euw2 (12:18)
sophia: What about autoscaler tuning — it looks like it reacted but not fast/orthogonally enough.
alex: We need an autoscaler rule to consider per-node mem headroom + in-flight RPC latency to cache store before placing many replicas on same AZ.
maria: Agreed. Proposed follow-ups (short):
1) Forecasting & traffic: update session-length forecasts with the marketing cohort delta and add an alert when observed median session length deviates >25% from forecast.
2) Autoscaler: add a placement constraint that factors mem_headroom and cache_eviction_lag per AZ, and a cool-down on AZ weight changes.
3) Cache eviction resiliency: add async eviction retries and quota-based eviction when network RTT spikes to cache store.
4) Network: ops to replace/upgrade the two suspect ToR switches in euw1 and enable better fanout telemetry.
5) Run a capacity drill: simulate 3x long-chat session traffic in euw1 during low traffic to validate autoscaler placements.

jamal: For commercial teams: what's the rough cost impact for the pool and do we need to buy more reserved capacity? I'm worried a repeat during Black Friday would be worse.
maria: Short answer: we didn't exceed reserved commitments, but unit cost rose because we spilled to on-demand euw2 capacity for ~40m. Ballpark additional cost: ~$18k for the spill window. If long-chat profile persists we should consider temporary reserved bump or enforce stricter concurrency caps for that campaign.
kai: Action owners: 
- maria: draft incident note and timeline for PMs + ops (today)
- alex: autoscaler rule prototype (this week)
- sophia: cache eviction changes + tests (next sprint)
- ops (jamal): vendor ticket for ToR switches + schedule replacement (ASAP)
- infra: run chaos drill (2 weeks)
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3487, assigned to eng-sre. Pager history attached.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout blocked for new long-chat model until autoscaler rule lands (flag set)
maria: Anything else? If not I'll convert this thread into a tidy incident summary and run it through post-incident checklist.
alex: Looks good. Please include the cost delta and the forecast adjustment in the summary.
jamal: Add a note to coordinate with marketing before major sends so we can pre-warm capacity or throttle cohorts.
sophia: I'll add a short regression test for cache eviction under high RTT.
kai: Thanks all. Closing the loop here — we have owners and short-term mitigations. I'll follow up on the autoscaler PR review.
